children: is working on a proprietary long/short program for tax-aware investing, the company's CEO said Thursday on its Q3 earnings call. The strategy has gained traction as wealthy investors seek to minimize their tax burdens.

"I do expect us to have an offering," Chairman and CEO Rick Wurster said. "We already have a great direct indexing capability today that has had wonderful performance in terms of tax alpha and delivering for clients, and I expect us to be able to deliver an extended version of that on long/short."

The opportunity is appealing "because we will be able to run that product in a very efficient way from a balance sheet and operational standpoint," he added. That will help the company to "sustain the ability to deliver long-short capabilities to our clients."

"It's certainly another way we can deliver monetization," Wurster noted. "And importantly, it's a way we can deliver sustainable long/short strategies to our clients in a way that is operationally and financially manageable over the longer term."
The company will provide updates about the offering on future calls, he added.

stock fell 1.9% in early afternoon trading.
